# Hopperlace

> Evaluation infrastructure for AI in high-stakes domains.

Hopperlace tells you when an AI system's decisions can be trusted and shows you why. We start where confident mistakes carry both societal and financial costs: high-stakes evidence work in life sciences. The first product is Evidence Synthesis AI, serving systematic review teams and pharmacovigilance / drug-safety teams monitoring literature for adverse events. The spine of the product is trust and governance: deference-aware evaluation, full reasoning per decision, and a complete audit trail.

## Product: Evidence Synthesis AI

Evidence Synthesis AI screens studies the way a careful expert would — decisive when it's confident, careful when it's not.

How it works:
- Handles the confident calls on its own — clear includes and excludes decided automatically where well-calibrated.
- Surfaces only the genuine judgment calls — ambiguous decisions routed to a human.
- Shows the reasoning behind every decision.
- Override anything, audit everything — the full log of human and AI decisions is auditable.

- Website: https://www.evidencesynthesisai.com/
- Status: Early pilots

## Why you can trust it

Validated across 6 frontier models and 5 medical domains — 2,729 studies, 16,374 screening decisions. No single model is uniformly safe; deference-aware evaluation is how you tell which decisions to trust.
- 45× error-rate gap between the best and worst model on their most-confident decisions — 99.7% vs 87.6% accurate.
- 3 independent metrics that converge on the same model ranking.

## Who it's for

- Systematic review teams: title-and-abstract screening without the year-long grind, with an audit trail that holds up to peer scrutiny.
- Pharmacovigilance / drug-safety teams: continuous literature monitoring for adverse events, with the documented decision trails.
- Research consultancies: evidence work at speed, with rigour you can defend to clients.

## Research

### Deference-Aware Evaluation for Human-in-the-Loop AI Systems
- Type: White Paper
- Date: 2026
- Authors: Hopperlace Research
- DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/A69YH
- Link: https://osf.io/a69yh/
- Also: Poster at the Workshop on Technical AI Governance Research (TAIGR), ICML 2026

Key finding: a model's confident-error rate can swing more than eightfold from one review to the next — which is why screening needs an evaluation layer that knows when its own judgments can be trusted.

## Team

- Yuyu Shen — Founder. A decade building production AI in regulated industries — fintech, employment, and consumer banking. Founded Hopperlace after recurring exposure to the same gap: AI deployed in high-stakes work without evaluation infrastructure capable of distinguishing trustworthy outputs from overconfident ones. Author of the deference-aware evaluation framework; poster at ICML 2026 TAIGR workshop.
- Martin Walker, MPH — Co-founder, Evidence Synthesis. Background in evidence-based health and systematic review evidence synthesis; brings the domain experience that keeps the system honest about clinical reality. Resident AI skeptic.

## Where we go next

Life sciences is where we start. But the problem of AI that doesn't know the limits of its own competence appears wherever consequential decisions rest on AI outputs. Hopperlace's methodology was built to travel.
